transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-20 16:30 PT / Duration ~62m / Recording: yes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Maria Chen (Sable Head of ML), Derek Cole (Platform), Priya Kapoor (Data Privacy), Omar Aziz (Product)
---
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm lena from redwood, i'll kick things off — marco will run the console and the eval demo. small agenda: prompt sets, regression alerts, a/b comparisons, and then Q&A about security and deployment options.
[00:18] Maria: great, thanks. we just finished a small POC with an open model, wanting to understand how we monitor drift and regression — and how to run controlled a/b experiments across models.
[00:28] Marco: perfect. i'll share my screen, sending the demo deck link in chat — https://redwood.ai/decks/eval-telemetry.pdf 
[00:40] Marco: okay, console home, this is the eval workspace we preloaded for sable - prompt-sets on the left, traffic stream, and the compare pane. first, prompt sets: you can group prompts by intent, add expected labels and scoring rubrics. we show pass/fail and continuous metrics.
[01:05] Derek: quick q — can we import our existing golden set from S3? our teams store test prompts in a bucket.
[01:12] Marco: yeah, you can import CSV/JSON from S3 or paste. we also accept webhooks for automated runs. for the pilot we'll import your bucket schema.
[01:22] Maria: how does the regression alerting work? we need to know when answers degrade on certain intents.
[01:28] Marco: there's two layers — baseline and rolling. baseline is a fixed checkpoint (eg: model v1.4 on date X). rolling uses a moving window. alerts fire on percentile drops or effect-size thresholds. you can choose absolute delta or statistical significance (p-values, bootstrap).
[01:50] Priya: is any user content leaving our VPC? data residency is critical, we can't send PII to hosted services without controls.
[01:59] Lena: totally hear that. we support three deployment modes: hosted (fastest), dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs under your tenancy logically isolated), and private (VPC or on-prem). with private, the inference plane sits in your network; control plane can be optional. we also have KMS/HSM integrations for envelope encryption and full audit logs.
[02:22] Priya: do you have SOC2 docs? and can we get an excerpt showing log retention and access controls?
[02:27] Lena: yes, we'll send the SOC2 attestation and a one-page security checklist right after.
[02:32] Marco: back to alerts — i'll show an example. here's a regression alert we triggered last week on 'claims summarization' intent. you can see the rubric: factuality score, hallucination flag, and latency. the alerts show affected prompts, significance, and suggested rollback candidates.
[03:00] [03:00] Speaker 1: um, can you lower the threshold so we don't get noise?
[03:04] Marco: yes, adjustable thresholds, and you can create suppression windows during deploys. also we support grouping alerts by intent owner so the right team gets paged.
[03:18] Maria: how do you handle A/B comparisons? we want to test two model families and traffic splits.
[03:25] Marco: the A/B lab creates paired evaluations on the same prompt-set. you can run paired statistical tests, compute lift on metrics like accuracy, safety, and latency. there's an experiment tab where you define splits, sample sizes, and success criteria.
[03:44] Omar: sample size calc — do you do power analysis? we're worried about noisy metrics.
[03:49] Marco: yes, built-in power analysis; it recommends sample size for target effect-size and confidence. it also suggests stratified sampling by user segment.
[03:56] Derek: latency/cost tradeoffs — if we run a high-quality quantized model in dedicated, does it still keep latency SLA? what's the typical p95 for summarization?
[04:06] Marco: p95 depends on sequence length and batching. for a 512 token context on A100 equivalent, we see p95 around 95–150 ms with our optimized kernels and continuous batching. with quantization (4-bit) you can get 2–3x cost reduction but may see slight quality delta; that's where A/B and regression checks come in.
[04:32] Priya: are KV cache and long-context handled in private? we have long-running chats and need correct token-level caching.
[04:40] Marco: yes, KV cache is supported across deployments. for private we recommend local persistent cache with eviction policies. we also expose per-request debug traces to inspect cache hits/misses.
[04:52] Maria: any good examples of alert noise reduction? we want only actionable alerts.
[04:56] Marco: two levers — rubric specificity (more granular metrics) and alert aggregation across prompt groups. also run automated hypothesis tests to reduce false positives.
[05:08] Lena: i'll flag that we can onboard with a pilot focusing on a small set of intents to tune thresholds before rolling out org-wide. reduces noise and gives measurable ROI.
[05:19] Derek: about integrations, can we push events into our existing PagerDuty and Slack?
[05:23] Marco: yep — webhook, pagerduty, opsgenie, slack. plus a REST API to pull raw eval results for downstream analytics.
[05:32] [05:32] Maria: show me the API flow for running a prompt-set programmatically.
[05:35] Marco: here's the API call: /v1/evals/run with body referencing prompt-set id and model variant. response includes per-prompt scores and a diff object for A/B. we also provide streaming to get progressive results for long jobs.
[05:50] [06:00] Speaker 2: (mumbling) do you log raw prompts?
[06:03] Lena: by default we persist minimal metadata and aggregate metrics in hosted. for customers requiring no raw prompt storage, private mode can be configured to never store raw prompts, or to encrypt them with your KMS and zero-access keys. that's a common enterprise pattern.
[06:25] Priya: retention window — can we set retention to 90 days and auto-purge?
[06:29] Marco: yes, retention policies are configurable per-tenant and per-dataset; we can also push retention events to your lifecycle controller.
[06:40] Maria: regarding drift — do you do embedding-based clustering to detect semantic drift? we have paraphrase-heavy inputs.
[06:47] Marco: we compute embedding centroids by intent and monitor distance shifts; combined with metric degradation it helps spot semantic drift. we also surface exemplar prompts that moved out of distribution.
[06:58] Omar: can we run canary rollouts where a subset of users see the new model and then auto-fallback if regressions exceed threshold?
[07:05] Marco: yes, that's built in. rollout policies allow canary percents, auto-fallback when a given metric crosses a threshold, and automatic rollback to previous pinned model.
[07:17] Derek: curious about cost attribution — how granular is token cost per route or per model?
[07:22] Marco: per-token cost is broken down by route and model; console shows token-level cost, batching savings, and cost per inference. you can also tag requests to attribute to product teams.
[07:35] Maria: who on your side will be our point for security?
[07:38] Lena: i'll own account setup and commercial, marco will do the technical deep-dive, and the security team can join for SOC2/KMS specifics. i'll share contact details.
[07:46] [07:46] Speaker 3: (background noise)
[07:48] Marco: next i'll demo an A/B compare run we did internally — results table, confidence intervals, effect size, and a visualization heatmap showing prompts that flipped labels.
[08:05] Marco: notice this 'flip rate' metric — it highlights prompts where outputs differed qualitatively; helpful for root-cause. you can flag those for manual review or auto-assign to an annotator queue.
[08:20] Maria: do you provide an annotation UI? our labeling is scattered.
[08:24] Marco: yes there is an integrated annotator interface for human labels, and we support exporting to your label toolchain or importing labeled sets back in.
[08:33] Priya: can you lock down RBAC so only compliance can view raw prompts?
[08:37] Marco: RBAC is role-based and integrates with SSO/SAML; fine-grained permissions can restrict raw prompt views to certain roles. audit logs show who accessed what and when.
[08:49] Derek: how long to get a pilot running? we prefer a two-week pilot to validate alerts and A/B flows.
[08:55] Lena: typical pilot is 1–3 weeks. we can provision a sandbox org, connect to your S3 bucket and a small dedicated pool, import your prompt-set, and run the A/B lab with your models.
[09:08] Maria: cost estimate? rough order of magnitude for two-week pilot including data ingress and small dedicated GPU?
[09:15] Lena: i'll send a tailored pilot pricing sheet — but rough O(4–10k) depending on GPU and throughput. we'll outline Dedicated vs Hosted price and the expected token volumes.
[09:27] Marco: one more note — Optimize suggests batching/quantization profiles by workload; it can recommend a quantization that keeps your rubric score within tolerance while reducing cost. that suggestion is based on historical evals.
[09:45] Maria: are those suggestions deterministic or heuristic? we need reproducibility for audits.
[09:51] Marco: suggestions are deterministic given a config hash and dataset snapshot; we record the experiment config so it can be audited and replayed.
[10:02] [10:02] Speaker 1: (crosstalk)
[10:05] Lena: wrapping up — recap: we'll share the security pack and SOC2, provision a sandbox pilot, marco will import your prompt-set and run an initial A/B with sample size calc, and we schedule an SE-only deep-dive about Private VPC.
[10:20] Maria: sounds good. a couple asks — can you include a sample alert policy template and an A/B experiment playbook?
[10:26] Lena: yes, we have a one-page playbook and an alert policy template — will attach.
[10:32] Derek: last thing, do you have any references in insurance or finance customers with similar compliance needs?
[10:37] Lena: yes, i'll include two case studies — one with an insurer and one with a regulated fintech.
[10:43] Maria: okay thanks, that was helpful.
[10:47] Marco: thanks all — we'll follow up with notes and the ticket items.
[10:50] [10:50] Meeting ended
